questions.q: By default, under what identity does a CmdExec job step run?
options: Anonymous/no identity at all
The Windows account of whoever created the job
The SQL Server Agent service account
The SQL Server Database Engine service account, always different from Agent's
questions.explain: Without a proxy, non-T-SQL subsystems like CmdExec run under the Agent service account's identity, which is often over-privileged for the specific task.

questions.q: What does a SQL Server CREDENTIAL object store?
options: A backup file's checksum
A job's schedule frequency codes
A Windows account's authentication information, encrypted, so SQL Server can present that identity externally
The SQL Server sysadmin password only
questions.explain: CREATE CREDENTIAL stores a Windows login and its secret (encrypted) so SQL Server can act as that identity when needed, such as for an Agent proxy.

questions.q: What naming requirement applies specifically to a credential used for an Agent proxy?
options: The credential must start with 'proxy_'
The credential must be named identically to the job
The credential's name must match the Windows account name itself
There is no naming requirement in any case
questions.explain: While credential names generally don't have to match the account, an Agent proxy specifically requires the credential to be named after the Windows account it wraps.

questions.q: Which stored procedure authorizes a proxy for use by a specific job step subsystem like CmdExec?
options: sp_grant_proxy_to_subsystem
sp_add_credential
sp_add_operator
sp_add_jobstep
questions.explain: sp_add_proxy creates the proxy from a credential, and sp_grant_proxy_to_subsystem is the separate call that authorizes it for a specific subsystem.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say many shops mandate proxies even for sysadmin-role DBAs, who are exempt from needing one?
options: Sysadmin members are technically incapable of running CmdExec steps
It has no real operational benefit — it's purely a checkbox for compliance audits
Proxies are required by SQL Server licensing terms
It forces every non-T-SQL step to run under an explicitly scoped identity instead of defaulting to whatever ambient privilege is available
questions.explain: The sysadmin exemption from needing a proxy is exactly why some shops require proxies anyway — it enforces least-privilege scoping instead of relying on ambient sysadmin rights.
